prompt:
Paint the COMPLETE top-down map of one outdoor area of a volcanic ash land in a fantasy JRPG world as ONE finished game map image, in rich premium modern hi-bit pixel art (hand-placed crisp square pixels, hue-shifted colour ramps, dark warm outlines, lush natural detail), classic top-down RPG map view seen from above with a slight 3/4 tilt (tree crowns, rocks and buildings seen from above with their south-facing sides visible; NOT an isometric view, NOT a diorama, no depth-of-field, no tilt-shift, no 3D render, no perspective).

THE PLACE: A BLACK-SAND BEACH ON A VOLCANIC COAST: steaming dark crags along the north with two gaps where paths come down; a wide beach of BLACK VOLCANIC SAND with drifts of grey ash; clusters of HEXAGONAL BASALT COLUMNS; warm turquoise tide pools; huge rounded grey-green rocks that look like giant TURTLE SHELLS; in the east a glowing LAVA FLOW runs down into the surf; shallow foamy water, then the dark blue sea along the south. Palette: jet-black sand, charcoal basalt, grey-green shell rocks, turquoise pools, white surf, deep blue sea, orange lava. Wild, primeval, strange.

The FIRST attached image is an exact LAYOUT GUIDE drawn on a 60 x 36 tile grid (each tile = 48 x 48 px of the output; the output is 2880 x 1728 px). Trace over it: your painting is laid pixel-for-pixel on top of it and used directly as the walkable game map, so every road, shore, cliff, tree mass, water body and landmark must sit exactly where it is in the guide at the same size (keep every edge within a few pixels of the guide; do not shift, shrink, mirror or re-arrange anything; keep the exact width of the roads and of the one- and two-tile gaps).

The SECOND attached image is only a STYLE REFERENCE from the same game: match its pixel-art rendering (pixel size, clusters, outlines, colour ramps, level of detail). Do NOT copy anything from it (no houses, towers, ponds, paths or objects from it).

The guide is soft colour-coding only (its blurred edges only mean the edge is natural and free-flowing): do NOT copy its flat colours, straight tile steps, circles or stripes. Interpret every area as the real material with rich natural variation, and give shores, woods, meadows and cliffs natural, organic, slightly irregular outlines (bulging or receding by at most a third of a tile around the guide edge). Make it feel like a real, exciting place to explore, full of small natural detail.

Guide colour key:
- mid grey = open VOLCANIC ASH ground (walkable): flat grey ash with small pebbles, footprints, a few dry tufts.
- pale grey soft areas = ASH DRIFTS (walkable): smooth low drifts of pale grey ash with wind ripples, outlines free-flowing and organic (never square or stepped), blending softly into the flat ash (low, walkable, no cliffs).
- dark grey with light swirl strokes = COOLED LAVA CRUST (walkable, FLAT GROUND): black-grey ropey pahoehoe lava lying level with the ash around it, flat folds and swirls, slight purple-grey sheen; it blends softly into the ash with ragged natural edges: NO raised edges, NO rims, NO walls, NO steps, NO plateaus.
- green = MOSS and hardy GRASS (walkable, flat).
- grey-olive with short strokes = dry ash-grey SCRUB GRASS (walkable, low).
- dusty tan band = the ROAD: packed ash and earth with ruts and small stones along its edges (walkable).
- darker brown = a narrow FOOTPATH of trodden earth (walkable).
- slate grey with block lines = BASALT PAVING / flagstones or mineral ledges (walkable, flat).
- turquoise = warm WATER: hot-spring pools / tide pools (not walkable).
- dull teal = SHALLOW foamy water at the shore (walkable wet sand and surf).
- deep blue = the SEA (not walkable): dark water, small waves, white surf where it meets the shore.
- bright orange with yellow cracks = molten LAVA (not walkable): glowing orange-yellow molten rock with dark crust plates, a thin dark cooled rim at its banks.
- black branching marks = CHARRED DEAD TREES (not walkable): bare black trunks and branches.
- grey-olive circles = small hardy BUSHES (not walkable).
- dark grey circles = BOULDERS of dark volcanic rock (not walkable).
- all colour areas are LEVEL GROUND unless listed as not walkable; only the crags below are raised.
- grey-brown with horizontal strata and a light top edge = CRAGS / rock cliffs (not walkable): jagged layered grey-brown volcanic rock dusted with ash on top, sheer faces facing south, fallen rocks at the foot.
Landmarks (paint each exactly on its block, at the block's size):
- the blocks in colour rgb(110,118,100) = huge rounded GREY-GREEN ROCKS whose cracked domed tops look exactly like giant TURTLE SHELLS half sunk in the black sand.
Walkable areas must stay walkable-looking: no boulders, trees, fences or objects standing on them unless the guide shows them.

Pixel art rules: crisp square pixels, no blur, no anti-aliasing, no painterly brush strokes, no noise, clear clusters, hue-shifted ramps. Characters in this game are about 72 output px tall, so details should be at that scale.
Lighting: this is the ALBEDO base layer (the game darkens it into night at runtime and adds lamp light on top). Neutral, soft, even daylight-like light as in the style reference; NO darkness, NO night tint, NO long cast shadows, NO light pools, NO glow halo (molten lava is painted bright orange as a material, but casts no light onto its surroundings), NO vignette, NO fog, NO clouds over the map.
Do NOT paint any characters, people, animals, monsters, birds, treasure chests, lanterns, lamp posts, torches, campfires, tents, signs, signposts, text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, borders, frames or UI. Those are added later as separate sprites: leave the ground open for them.
revised_prompt:
Create the ONE COMPLETE finished volcanic black-sand-beach JRPG game map image, using the FIRST attached 2880×1728 image as a STRICT pixel-registered layout underpainting, and the SECOND attached image ONLY for pixel-art rendering style. Output the same 60×36 tile frame, 48 px/tile, landscape 5:3 aspect. This is an image-to-image tracing task: preserve the exact map positions, footprints and widths of every feature in first image, never reinterpret the composition or move, mirror, scale features. Render premium modern high-bit PIXEL ART: actual hand-arranged crisp square-pixel clusters, intricate readable detailing, warm dark outlines and hue-shifted ramps, no smooth rendering, antialiasing, filter, 3D or isometric projection. Orthographic classic RPG straight-down overhead with slight south-facing surfaces for cliffs and rocks. Neutral evenly lit albedo, no directional shadows, atmospheric effects or lava illumination.

Specifically reproduce the FIRST guide's layout: rocky high crags occupy the north border across the entire width but have their TWO precise narrow breaks in the top edge near x=335 and x=2450, and the irregular bottom of the northern cliff falls to y~200–335; render stratified jagged dark brown-grey basalt crag faces facing south with pale ash lip, loose scree at their feet; don't block either gap. Preserve four small separate rectilinear cliff outcrops at approximately (x=815–960,y=432–575), (1775–1965,530–670), (1295–1390,960–1055), (2160–2305,865–1010), converting angular schematic linework into natural basalt crags without moving their footprints. Huge mainly wide uninterrupted LEVEL walkable charcoal-black ash beach from crags to surf, scattered tiny pebbles and ash ripples, areas of smooth naturally feathered grey ash drifts at precisely the guide's lighter soft-shaded patches; the sinuous subtle brown/grey variation shown across upper left and center is ground, not a raised barrier. Place THREE giant cracked grey-green TURTLE-SHELL-SHAPED DOMED ROCKS half buried in black sand EXACTLY on the three grey-olive blocks: near (695,840), (1295,790), (2060,1080), each constrained to guide block size; make identifiable shell-panel polygon cracking and rounded domed texture. Small existing dark volcanic boulders where circles are drawn, including pair on west and right-of-center; don't invent obstructions on open walkable areas. Two turquoise tide pools in exact small areas near (520,1050) and (1590,1170), foamy delicate edge. South edge shallow dull teal wet surf band follows guide boundary around y~1160–1380 with center variations, white foamy wavering shore line; dark indigo sea occupies bottom y~1300–1728 and carries scattered tiny pixel-cluster wave crests. At far EAST a single uninterrupted skinny molten lava flow occupying same location and exact meandering width as the vivid orange strip from x~2700 top to x~2710 bottom, meeting the sea: rich bright orange/yellow molten interiors, thin dark cooled banks, little dark crust plates, no outward glow and no widened river. Preserve all negative-space traversable clear ash, including beach between sea and northern cliffs. Convert guide flat color encoding into realistic organic material while keeping coast, boulders, pools, crags, shell rocks, lava pixel-accurate within few pixels where possible. Palette black graphite ash, charcoal and subtle purple-black basalt, grey-green shell stone, aqua tidewater, white foam, deep navy sea, bright orange lava. Lush fine naturalistic environmental detail at the scale of ~72 pixel characters, but no added landmarks. No characters, animals, structures, buildings, paved city, text, grid, borders or interface.
